key_insight: Agent harness logic can be externalized as editable, executable natural-language artifacts (Natural-Language Agent Harnesses, NLAHs), making harness design transparent, portable, and comparable across agents and runtimes.
problem_solved: Harness engineering is typically buried in controller code and runtime conventions, which makes harnesses hard to transfer, reproduce, compare, and study as first-class scientific objects.
method: Encode high-level control and evaluation policies for agents as natural-language harness specifications (NLAHs) that are human-editable.
Provide an execution/interpretation layer that maps these NL specifications to runtime behavior so they can be applied across different controllers and environments.
Empirically evaluate NLAHs to demonstrate improved portability, transparency, and comparability of harness behavior across agents and tasks.
impact: NLAHs lower the barrier to sharing, iterating on, and benchmarking agent harnesses, improving reproducibility and enabling systematic study and comparison of agent control strategies for AI/ML practitioners and evaluators.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: NLAH (text) → Interpreter/Runtime → Agent / Environment
Before vs After comparison: code-embedded harnesses (opaque) vs NLAHs (editable & portable)
Flowchart: author edits NLAH → run across multiple agents → collect comparable metrics
Icon set: editability, portability, reproducibility, benchmarking
paper_authors: Linyue Pan, Lexiao Zou, Shuo Guo, Jingchen Ni, Hai-Tao Zheng
